speaker: client
text: Thanks for accepting the invitation, Luka. By 2031-06-15, I’ll send you an initial overview covering 6 boards. We can then discuss the boards, and I’d appreciate your comments, especially about any wrong decisions we should fix.

speaker: freelancer
text: Sure, that works for me.

speaker: client
text: Please review this document for the first of 6 boards and let me know whether the design makes sense to you.

speaker: freelancer
text: Would it cause any problems if I waited until next Tuesday to review the PDF?

speaker: client
text: That is no problem. Since I just made five changes, I’ll post V6 of the document; please download the latest version next Tuesday before reviewing it.

speaker: freelancer
text: Thanks; I’ll hold off until you have uploaded the modified document.

speaker: freelancer
text: The document review is complete, and we can discuss the project whenever you are free.

speaker: client
text: We can use this chat for the discussion. What are your thoughts on the project overall and on this first power PCB?

speaker: freelancer
text: For the Power board, it may be worth adding TVS ESD protection.

speaker: freelancer
text: For safety, the battery should have protection as well as a fifth NTC terminal.

speaker: client
text: Thank you for the suggestion; we can add that. Please also propose any further changes you think are needed.

speaker: freelancer
text: One point I’m uncertain about is the boost converter: is the plan to disable it through the EN pin to prevent battery drain?

speaker: freelancer
text: Please make sure the physical length of the I2C connections receives attention.

speaker: client
text: By battery protection, are you referring to a hard short circuit across the battery terminals? Overcharge is already handled by the AXP2101, which cuts off at 4.45V, and its overdischarge cutoff is configurable at about ~2.4V. As for NTC, yes, we should add it to J\_BAT.

speaker: freelancer
text: Yes, I was referring to thermal protection rather than hard-short protection, because the component supports that too.

speaker: client
text: All the suggestions so far look good, thank you. I still need to update the document with them.

speaker: client
text: For the boost converter, connect EN to GPIO3 rather than tying it HIGH, so I can switch it off and on programmatically.

speaker: client
text: That boost-control change will be added to the document.

speaker: freelancer
text: Will deep-sleep mode be used by the ESP32?

speaker: client
text: With I2C interboard cables limited to ≤30cm, the setup should work at 800kHz using the existing 4.4kΩ pull-ups.

speaker: client
text: At present, the ESP32 runs at 240MHz max and drops to 120MHz while idle through automatic light sleep. It enters deep sleep at about ~35µA only when the battery is critical or after a false wake. The wake sources are a 20min timer and the touch button on GPIO 26 ext0. In the final version, however, I will keep it in deep sleep most of the time and wake it only for updates. Does that mean some pins need to move, perhaps AXP IRQ?

speaker: client
text: Should we also reconsider the boost EN pin?

speaker: freelancer
text: In that case, adding a pull-down resistor to the boost converter’s EN pin might be better.

speaker: client
text: All your suggested updates are being incorporated into the v8 I’m preparing, and I’ll take the pull-down proposal into account as well. Thanks.

speaker: client
text: A 330kΩ pull-down has now been placed on MT3608 EN.

speaker: freelancer
text: Until the ESP32 enables it, the boost converter will therefore remain off.

speaker: client
text: Yes—the boost converter supplies the sensors that require 5V.

speaker: client
text: Those sensors will operate only periodically rather than running continuously.

speaker: freelancer
text: Yes, operating them periodically will lower battery consumption.

speaker: client
text: Please review V8 and let me know if you have any further suggestions; everything you have proposed so far has been very helpful.

speaker: freelancer
text: I'll check the updated document.

speaker: client
text: Should I begin the Hire process? I’m ready to do so on 2031-06-15.

speaker: freelancer
text: Apologies, it's been a long day.

speaker: freelancer
text: What completion date do you need for this part of the project?

speaker: client
text: Although there is no hard deadline, completing it sooner would of course be preferable, as always.

speaker: freelancer
text: Could you give me at least an approximate completion target?

speaker: client
text: Since I really don't know how much time this normally requires, I was hoping for delivery within a few days. Please tell me if that expectation is unrealistic.

speaker: freelancer
text: To plan around my other projects, I need to know whether I can finish on time; a couple of days is workable.

speaker: client
text: If a couple of days is the turnaround for each board, that works for me.

speaker: freelancer
text: Ok

speaker: client
text: I’ll proceed with the hire by clicking the button right away.

speaker: freelancer
text: Thanks; I’m glad to take on the project.

speaker: client
text: You're welcome. I confirmed your offer exactly as submitted and completed the hire.

speaker: client
text: Before you begin, here is V7. The I2C pull-ups were removed from this board because they have been moved to the main board, and that is the revision’s only change.

speaker: freelancer
text: Anything you think could be useful, please post here.

speaker: freelancer
text: Since the HRO TYPE-C-31-M-17 is 6p and has no D+ or D- data lines, the USB connector must be replaced.

speaker: client
text: A standard, readily sourced connector is fine; just make sure it is easy to obtain. If it is available on AliExpress, that is a sufficient check.

speaker: freelancer
text:
Would the following part work as the replacement?
<https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C2760486.html?s_z=n_HRO%2520TYPE-C-31-M-%252017>

speaker: client
text: Availability is my only concern. This premium option normally costs 1.46$, while typical ones are 0.4$; we can use it provided compatible alternatives exist if it goes out of stock, since I do not want a part that may be unavailable regularly.

speaker: freelancer
text: Can you provide the PCB shape and connector locations, and confirm whether PCB mounting holes are required?

speaker: client
text: Inside the case, the board will lie horizontally, with the USB protruding slightly from the shorter edge. For mounting, 8 holes at the corners will be enough.

speaker: freelancer
text: Dimensions, shape?

speaker: client
text: Keep the board as small as the components permit, with USB-C on the shorter edge and 8 mounting holes sized M2.5 at the corners. A roughly 4:2 aspect ratio is preferred; it should not be square.

speaker: freelancer
text: To let you review the design and identify any changes, I'll send the files within 3 days. I also need to know which kind of LED should provide the battery-charge indication.

speaker: client
text: Battery-charge status should be shown by the SK6812 addressable LED chain on GPIO13, which is on the main board. No separate LED is needed; thank you for clarifying the LED requirement.

speaker: client
text: From what I can see so far, it looks great, and I think that is everything. Thanks; once I receive the files, I can inspect them more closely.

speaker: freelancer
text: For the design, which connectors would you like me to use?

speaker: freelancer
text: Which arrangement should I follow—the first picture or the second one?

speaker: client
text: Use the vertical JST arrangement shown in the first picture. I have one concern because this assembly will plug into a base, so I'll send an image now to explain it more easily.

speaker: freelancer
text: Ok

speaker: client
text: Plugging it in with this orientation would prevent me from connecting the battery underneath.

speaker: client
text: Because the support is currently 3d printed and there are now 8 holes, I could make a different support that uses screws to secure it. However, it still has to fit vertically in this orientation.

speaker: freelancer
text: Vertically, like those green PCBs?

speaker: client
text: Ideally, the battery JST would sit next to the board JST, with both vertical, as shown in AM\_1.

speaker: freelancer
text: I believe I understand it.

speaker: client
text: This arrangement is perfect provided it fits, leaves at least a small gap between the connectors, and does not cover the holes.

speaker: freelancer
text: It is being shown solely for illustrative purposes.

speaker: client
text: Since I understand that it is only illustrative, the proposed concept is perfect.

speaker: freelancer
text: There is not enough room for the connectors to fit within 68mm.

speaker: freelancer
text: With holes

speaker: client
text: Given that fit issue, the battery connector can instead go on the back, opposite the usb-c.

speaker: client
text: For J\_BAT, did you use a 2.0mm JST-PH connector with 2 pins or 3 pins?

speaker: client
text: Should it instead use the documented 5-pin JST-GH connector with a 1.25mm pitch?

speaker: freelancer
text: The confirmed count is 5p.

speaker: freelancer
text: JST-GH uses a 1.25mm pitch.
